questions.stem:
In a school canteen, students can choose from a main course of meat ($M$), fish ($F$) or vegetarian ($V$). They can then choose a drink of either water ($W$) or juice ($J$).

The partially completed tree diagram, where $p$ and $q$ are probabilities, shows the probabilities of these choices for a randomly selected student.

[Tree diagram: Main course branches Meat (0.40), Fish (0.35), Vegetarian (……); from Meat: Drink branches Water ($p$), Juice (……); from Fish: Drink branches Water ($q$), Juice (……); from Vegetarian: Drink branches Water (0.40), Juice (……)]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Complete the tree diagram, giving your answers in terms of $p$ and $q$ where appropriate.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: 0.25 for P($V$)
B1: correct probabilities on 2nd branches $(1-p)$, $(1-q)$ [allow their values] and 0.6

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find an expression, in terms of $p$ and $q$, for the probability that a randomly selected student chooses water to drink.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) B1ft: $\mathrm{P}(W) = 0.4p + 0.35q + "0.25"\times 0.4$ [$= 0.4p+0.35q+0.1$] for a correct expression using their values from tree diagram

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The events "choosing a vegetarian main course" and "choosing water to drink" are independent.
(c) Find a linear equation in terms of $p$ and $q$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: correct expression: $\mathrm{P}(W\cap V) = "0.1" = "0.25"\times \mathrm{P}(W)$ or $\mathrm{P}(W) = \mathrm{P}(W|V) = 0.4$, for sight or use of a correct expression in $V$ and $W$ or correct equation in $p$ and $q$ (ft their part (b))
A1: for a fully correct equation (needn't be simplified) [may see $0.4p+0.35q=0.3$ or $8p+7q=6$]

parts.label: d
parts.text:
A student who has chosen juice to drink is selected at random. The probability that they chose fish for their main course is $\frac{7}{30}$
(d) Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: for using given conditional probability to form an equation in $q$ and P($J$) using $\frac{7}{30}$: $\frac{7}{30} = \frac{0.35(1-q)}{"\mathrm{P}(J)"}$
dM1: (dep on 1st M1) for getting P($J$) = 0.6 or sub $1-$their (b) to get 2nd equation in $p$ and $q$ [May see $8p-23q+12=0$]
Since $V$ and $W$ are independent so are $V$ and $W' = J$ so P($J$) = 0.6
A1: [So $1-q = \frac{2}{3}\mathrm{P}(J)$ therefore] $q=0.6$
$8p+7\times"0.6" = 6$
ddM1: (dep on both Ms) for seeing substitution of their 1st value to find the 2nd value ($p$ or $q$). Allow ft of their $p$ or $q$ in one of their equations provided $p$ and $q$ both lie in $(0,1)$
A1: so $p=0.225$ or exact equivalent. After the 2nd M1, sight of $p=0.225$ and $q=0.6$ earns the final 3 marks
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st A1 for $q = 0.6$ [NB must be $q = 0.6$ not just P($J$) = 0.6] May see after 3rd M1 for solving with $p$

parts.label: e
parts.text:
The canteen manager claims that students who choose water to drink are most likely to choose a fish main course.
(e) State, showing your working clearly, whether or not the manager's claim is correct.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) {P($V|W$) = P($V$) = 0.25 (since independent) and P($M|W$) = 0.225 (=$p$)}
M1: $\mathrm{P}(F|W) = \frac{0.35\times"0.6"}{"0.4"}$ or $\frac{0.35q}{(b)}$ for a method for finding P($F|W$)
A1: $= \frac{21}{40}$ or 0.525 for a correct value $\frac{21}{40}$ or exact equivalent
B1ft: [Since this prob > 0.5 therefore it must be the largest] so conclusion is correct, for a correct conclusion based on enough probs found ft their probabilities. Allow B1ft for comparing 3 calculated probs of the form P($M\cap W$) needn't be correct ft

questions.stem:
The distance achieved in a long jump competition by students at a school is normally distributed with mean 3.8 metres and standard deviation 0.9 metres.

Students who achieve a distance greater than 4.3 metres receive a medal.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the proportion of students who receive medals.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) [$D$ = distance achieved] M1: $\mathrm{P}(D>4.3) = \mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{4.3-3.8}{0.9}\right)$ or P($Z>0.555\ldots$)
M1: $= 1-0.7123$ (tables)
A1: $= 0.2877$ (tables) or $0.289257\ldots$ (calc) awrt 0.288 or awrt 0.289
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for standardising 4.3 with 3.8 and 0.9 (allow $\pm$)
- 2nd M1 for $1 - p$ (where $0.7 < p < 0.8$)
- A1 for awrt 0.288 or 0.289 (calc. 0.289257) (correct answer only 3/3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The school wishes to give a certificate of achievement or a medal to the 80% of students who achieve a distance of at least $d$ metres.
(b) Find the value of $d$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $\frac{d-3.8}{0.9} = -0.8416$ (calc $-0.84162123\ldots$)
B1: for $z=\pm 0.8416$ or better used
A1: $d = 3.0425\ldots$ awrt 3.04
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for standardising with $d$, 3.8 and 0.9 and setting equal to a $z$ value $0.8 < |z| < 0.9$
- A1 for awrt 3.04 (condone $d \geqslant$ ...)
- Ans only: For awrt 3.0425 or 3.0426 score 3/3 For awrt 3.04 score M1B0A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Of those who received medals, the $\frac{1}{3}$ who jump the furthest will receive gold medals.
(c) Find the shortest distance, $g$ metres, that must be achieved to receive a gold medal.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $\mathrm{P}(D>g|D>4.3) = \frac{\mathrm{P}(D>g)}{\mathrm{P}(D>4.3)}$ or (a) $\left[=\frac{1}{3}\right]$ (o.e.), for either expression for the conditional prob. [or sight of $\frac{1}{3}$(a)] (ft their answer to (a) to 2 sf)
A1ft: $\therefore \mathrm{P}(D>g) = \frac{1}{3}(a) = 0.096419\ldots$ for P($D>g$) = 0.096 or better (0.289 gives 0.09633... calc 0.096419...). The P($D>g$) may be clearly shown on a diagram
dM1: (dep on 1st M1) $\frac{g-3.8}{0.9} = 1.302228\ldots$ for standardising with $g$, 3.8 and 0.9 and put equal to a $z$ value where $|z|>1$
A1: so $g=4.97200\ldots$ awrt 4.97 or awrt 4.98 (Correct answer with no incorrect working seen 4/4) (condone $g\geqslant\ldots$)
SC (Medals v Certificates): 1st B1 for [P($D>g$)=] $\frac{1}{3}\times 0.8 = \frac{4}{15}$ or 0.267 (score as 1st M0 1st A1); 2nd B1 for $g$ = awrt 4.36 (4.358 tables, 4.3606..calc) (score as 2nd M0 2nd A1)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1A1 can be awarded for P($D > g$) = $\frac{1}{3}$(a) or for P($D < g$) = 1 – $\frac{1}{3}$(a) [ft their (a) to 2 sf]

parts.label: d
parts.text:
A journalist from the local newspaper interviews a randomly selected group of 3 medal winners.
(d) Find the exact probability that there is at least one gold medal winner in the group.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: $\mathrm{P}(\text{no gold medals}) = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3$ for a correct probability of no gold medals or 2 of: $3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2\times\frac{1}{3}$ or $3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2\times\frac{2}{3}$ or $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^3$
M1: $\mathrm{P}(\text{at least one gold}) = 1-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3$ for $1-p^3$ or $3(p)^2(1-p)+3p(1-p)^2+(1-p)^3$ where $0<p<1$
A1: $= \frac{19}{27}$ (or exact equivalent) only e.g. $0.\dot{7}0\dot{3}$

questions.stem:
A group of students took some tests. A teacher is analysing the average mark for each student. Each student obtained a different average mark.

For these average marks, the lower quartile is 24, the median is 30 and the interquartile range (IQR) is 10
The three lowest average marks are 8, 10 and 15.5 and the three highest average marks are 45, 52.5 and 56

The teacher defines an outlier to be a value that is either

more than $1.5\times$ IQR below the lower quartile or
more than $1.5\times$ IQR above the upper quartile

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Determine any outliers in these data.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: Upper quartile = 34
M1: Lower limit $= 24-15=9$ or upper limit is "34"$+15=49$
A1ft, A1ft: So outliers are: 8, 52.5 and 56 (2nd A1ft for the lower outlier at 8 ft their limit provided limit $\leqslant 12$; 3rd A1ft for upper outliers at 52.5 and 56 ft their limit provided it is $>45$). NB these accuracy marks are for the outliers not the limits
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for $Q_3$ = 34 either stated or used/implied (score if seen on box plot)
- M1 for one correct calculation (ft their 34 for upper limit) [ May be implied by correct outliers]
- Award if their outliers are seen on box plot

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) On the grid below draw a box plot for these data, indicating clearly any outliers.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: for a box with $Q_1=24$, $Q_2=30$, $Q_3=$ their 34 and two whiskers one on each side
B1: for one lower whisker ending at 10 (or their 9) and outlier at 8 only
B1: for one upper whisker ending at 45 (or their 49 to match "9") and outliers at 52.5 and 56 only
SC Extra whiskers: If one set of whiskers gives a correct box plot award B1B0B0. Usual accuracy for plots – to within 0.5 of a square

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Use the quartiles to describe the skewness of these data.
Give a reason for your answer.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $Q_2-Q_1 (=6) > ("4"=)Q_3-Q_2$ or e.g. in words e.g. "$Q_3$ closer to $Q_2$ than $Q_1$ is", for correct comparison of $Q_2-Q_1$ and $Q_3-Q_2$ (ft their $Q_3$) (if no values seen must see comparison otherwise accept correctly assigned 6 and 4 without $>$)
A1ft: So negative (skew), for correct deduction based on their $Q_3$ (+ve skew if their $Q_3>36$, no skew if their $Q_3=36$)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Two more students also took the tests. Their average marks, which were both less than 45, are added to the data and the box plot redrawn.

The median and the upper quartile are the same but the lower quartile is now 26
(d) Redraw the box plot on the grid below.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: IQR now "34"$-26=8$ so new outlier limits are $26-1.5\times"8" = 14$ and "34"$+1.5\times"8"=46$, for recognising new IQR and at least one correct new limit (ft their 34, implied by correct plot)
A1ft: for a correct lower whisker ending at 15.5 (or their 14) and 2 correct outliers at 8 and 10
A1: for a fully correct box plot with upper whisker to 45 (or could go to 46 [to match their 14])
SC Extra whiskers: If one set of whiskers gives a correct box plot award M1A0A1

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) Give ranges of values within which each of these students' average marks must lie.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) [$Q_1$ has increased so both above 24 Median same so either side of or on median] B1: So one between 26 and 30 inc, allow that (…) (o.e. eg between 26 and 30)
[$Q_3$ unchanged so must be either side of $Q_3$] B1: so one between "34" and 45 inc, condone […] or (…) (ft their 34 and allow o.e. e.g. between 34 and 45)
